title: Nevada's 3rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Nevada's 3rd Congressional District pits Democratic incumbent Rep. Susie Lee against Republican nominee Marty O'Donnell, a video game composer best known for the Halo and Destiny franchises. The district, which covers western Las Vegas and parts of unincorporated Clark County, is considered a swing seat; Lee won re-election in 2024 by just 2.8 percentage points even as Donald Trump narrowly carried the district. The race is rated Lean Democratic by the Cook Political Report and is a key pickup opportunity for Republicans seeking to flip control of the U.S. House.
polling_note: No public opinion polls for this specific race were found as of the research date. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Lean Democratic but this is a race rating, not a poll.

candidates.name: Susie Lee
candidates.summary: Susie Lee is the Democratic incumbent representing Nevada's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2018. A former education nonprofit leader who founded After School All Stars and served as President of Communities in Schools of Nevada, she has been ranked the most bipartisan member of Congress and serves on the House Appropriations Committee. Lee won her competitive district by 2.8 points in 2024 and has a strong focus on affordable health care, public education, and economic development.

career_history.title: U.S. Representative
career_history.description: Represents Nevada's 3rd Congressional District; serves on House Appropriations Committee; member of Problem Solvers Caucus and New Democrats Coalition.

career_history.title: President
career_history.description: Led education nonprofit working to reduce dropout rates.

candidates.name: Marty O'Donnell
candidates.summary: Marty O'Donnell is the Republican nominee for Nevada's 3rd Congressional District, having won the June 9, 2026 primary with 42.3% of the vote. A veteran video game music composer best known for creating the iconic Halo and Destiny soundtracks, he earned a Master of Music degree from USC and founded the commercial music production company O'Donnell/Salvatori Inc. O'Donnell, who moved to Las Vegas in 2021, is running on a platform focused on border security, fiscal responsibility, and reducing the size of government, and has been endorsed by President Donald Trump.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling exists, so this forecast relies entirely on contextual factors. Democratic incumbent Susie Lee has won this swing district in three consecutive cycles, most recently by 2.8 points in 2024 while Donald Trump narrowly carried the district — demonstrating crossover appeal that is important in a presidential-year electorate. The Cook Political Report rates the race Lean Democratic, consistent with Lee's incumbency advantage, bipartisan reputation (ranked most bipartisan member of Congress), and seat on the Appropriations Committee. Republican nominee Marty O'Donnell is a high-profile first-time candidate (video game composer with Trump endorsement) who won a competitive primary with 42.3%, but lacks political experience and moved to Nevada only in 2021. 2026 is a presidential election year, which may reduce ticket-splitting compared to 2024, but the district's swing nature and Republican targeting make it genuinely competitive. Lee retains a modest but meaningful advantage; confidence is medium due to the complete absence of any public polling.
